title: The persona claim block still lets two consumers correlate
description:
Pseudonyms are now per-consumer and unlinkable, but the token around them is not. persona-grpc/src/service.rs builds a persona claim block carrying root_trust_domain, sources, auth_methods and a whole-second attested_at. Those values are identical for any two consumers served in the same window.

So two colluding consumers holding different pseudonyms can still infer they are talking to the same person by comparing that tuple. attested_at at second granularity is the strongest of the four: it is effectively a join key for concurrent requests.

They cannot recover the root identity — that is fixed, and the log no longer carries the mapping either. This is correlation, not deanonymisation. But README, SPEC-HIA and MOTIVATIONS all say two applications cannot work out they are talking to the same person, and as written that is now narrowly false.

Raised by the judge during persona-5s4b.41 and deliberately not fixed there: narrowing the claim block is a wire-format decision, and doing it inside a plumbing change would have been scope creep. The docs now state the residual explicitly rather than implying it is absent.

Options for whoever takes it: drop root_trust_domain (a consumer does not need it), coarsen or remove attested_at, and consider whether sources and auth_methods belong in a per-consumer token at all — they describe the human's environment, not the consumer's relationship to it. Note persona-ogiv wants attested_at to become MORE precise for freshness, which pulls the other way; the two need deciding together.
